content.en: The **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** is a mandatory requirement under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**. Banks are required to hold a portion of their **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** in the form of cash with the RBI. This ensures that banks maintain a minimum level of liquidity to meet withdrawal demands and allows the central bank to regulate the overall money supply in the Indian economy.

definition.en: Higher CRR reduces the lendable resources of banks, thereby tightening liquidity.
definition.hi: Higher CRR reduces the lendable resources of banks, thereby tightening liquidity.

content.en: Net Demand and Time Liabilities represent the base on which the CRR percentage is calculated.

content.en: Students often confuse CRR with Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR). Remember that CRR is kept with the RBI, while SLR is maintained by the bank itself.
